q: 1. The load, required to produce a unit deflection in a spring is called :
explain: Stiffness ($k$) is defined as Force per unit displacement ($F/\delta$).

q: 2. When a load on the free end of a cantilever beam is increased, failure will occur
options: in the middle of the beam
at a distance 2l/3 from free end
explain: For a cantilever, bending moment is maximum at the fixed (built-in) support, so failure (due to maximum bending stress) will initiate there.

q: 3. In approximate analysis of building frames under lateral loads, the point of contraflexure in columns is assumed at
explain: Methods like the Portal and Cantilever methods assume the point of zero moment (contraflexure) is at the mid-height of the column.

q: 4. A one dimensional structure is one in which
options: one dimension is very small and other two are large
one dimension is much larger than the other two dimensions
all the three dimensions are equal
explain: A one-dimensional structure (like a beam or column) has its length dimension much larger than its cross-sectional dimensions.

q: 5. A two dimensional structure is one in which
options: two dimensions are very much larger than the third
two dimensions are very much smaller than the third
explain: A two-dimensional structure (like a slab or wall) has two dimensions (length and width) much larger than the third (thickness).

q: 6. A beam is a
explain: A beam's length is much larger than its cross-sectional dimensions, classifying it as a one-dimensional structure.

q: 7. A slab is a
explain: A slab has length and width much larger than its thickness, classifying it as a two-dimensional structure.

q: 8. The bending moment diagram for a simply supported beam loaded in its centre is
explain: For a simply supported beam with a central point load, the BMD is a symmetric (isosceles) triangle peaking at midspan.

q: 9. The shear force diagram for a simply supported beam carrying a uniformly distributed load of w per unit length, consists of
explain: For a UDL on a simply supported beam, shear force varies linearly from +wl/2 to −wl/2, forming two right-angled triangles (positive on one half, negative on the other).

q: 10. In a simply supported beam carrying uniformly distributed load w per unit length, the point of contraflexure
options: lies in the centre of the beam
lies at the ends of the beam
depends upon the length of beam
explain: A simply supported beam under UDL has a bending moment that is always sagging (positive) throughout its span, never changing sign, so no point of contraflexure exists.

q: 11. The point of contraflexure occurs in
explain: Overhanging beams typically have both sagging (within supports) and hogging (over the overhang) moments, so the bending moment changes sign, creating a point of contraflexure.

q: 12. A beam of T-section is subjected to a shear force of F. The maximum shear force will occur at the
explain: As with most sections, the maximum shear stress in a T-section occurs at the neutral axis, where the parabolic shear distribution peaks within the web.

q: 13. A flitched beam is used to
options: change the shape of the beam
equalize the strength in tension and compression
increase the cross-section of the beam
explain: A flitched beam (composite timber-and-steel beam) is used to equalize/balance the strength characteristics in tension and compression by combining materials with complementary properties.

q: 14. A rectangular beam of length l supported at its two ends carries a central point load W. The maximum deflection occurs
explain: For a simply supported beam under a symmetric central point load, maximum deflection (by symmetry) occurs exactly at the midspan (centre).

q: 15. The moment diagram for a cantilever whose free end is subjected to a bending moment, will be a
explain: A pure moment applied at the free end of a cantilever produces a constant bending moment throughout its length, giving a rectangular BMD.

q: 16. If he shear force long a section of a beam is zero, the bending moment at the section is
explain: Since dM/dx = Shear Force, a zero shear force at a section indicates the bending moment is at a local extreme (maximum or minimum) at that point.

q: 17. A cantilever beam rectangular in cross-section is subjected to an isolated load at its free end. If the width of the beam is doubled, the deflection of the free end will be changed in the ratio of
explain: Since deflection δ ∝ 1/I and I ∝ b (width) for a rectangular section, doubling the width halves the deflection.

q: 18. The ratio of the maximum deflections of a simply supported beam with a central load W and of a cantilever of same length and with a load W at its free end is
explain: Comparing WL³/48EI (simply supported, central load) to WL³/3EI (cantilever, end load) gives a ratio of (1/48)/(1/3) = 1/16.

q: 19. When a single load W moves over a simply supported beam, the maximum bending moment at a section will occur when the load is placed
explain: For a single moving load, the bending moment at a given section is maximum precisely when that load is positioned directly over the section itself.

q: 20. In a rigid jointed frame, the joints are considered
options: to rotate only as a whole
that 50% of members rotate in clockwise direction and 50% in anti clockwise direction
explain: At a rigid joint, all connected members are assumed to rotate together by the same angle (the joint rotates as a whole, maintaining the rigid angles between members).

q: 21. For a beam of uniform strength, if depth is constant
explain: For a rectangular section with constant depth d, since σ ∝ M/(bd²), keeping stress constant with fixed d requires width b to vary directly proportional to M.

q: 22. In the case of H section the maximum shear stress will occur at
options: at the junction of the web and flanges
explain: For an H-section (similar to I-section), there's a notable jump in shear stress at the web-flange junction due to the abrupt change in width, often making this location critical.

q: 23. A straight beam subjected to pure bending will be bending in the shape of
explain: Under pure (constant) bending moment, the curvature 1/R = M/EI is constant along the length, causing the beam to deform into a circular arc.

q: 24. The expression EI d⁴y/dx⁴ at any section for a beam is equal to
explain: Differentiating the beam bending equation EI(d²y/dx²)=M twice gives EI(d⁴y/dx⁴) = d²M/dx² = load intensity (since dM/dx=V and dV/dx=-w), so this expression equals the load intensity at the section.

q: 25. Which of the following sections is the most efficient in carrying bending moments?
explain: An I-section concentrates most material in the flanges, far from the neutral axis, maximizing the section modulus for a given area, making it the most efficient shape in bending.

q: 26. The maximum deflection due to uniformly distributed load w per unit length over entire span of a cantilever of length l and of flexural rigidity EI is
explain: The standard formula for maximum (tip) deflection of a cantilever under UDL over its full length is wl⁴/8EI.

q: 27. The maximum deflection of a simply supported beam of span L, carrying an isolated load at the center of the span
explain: The standard formula for maximum deflection of a simply supported beam under a central point load W is WL³/48EI.

q: 28. The ratio of the deflections of the free end of a cantilever due to an isolated load at 1/3rd and 2/3rd of the span is
explain: Using the standard cantilever deflection formula for a load at distance a from the fixed end (deflection at tip involves a²(3L-a)), evaluating for a=L/3 versus a=2L/3 and taking the ratio gives 2/7.

q: 29. Ties are load carrying members of a frame, which are subjected to
explain: A tie is a truss/frame member specifically subjected to axial tension loads.

q: 30. Beams of uniform strength are preferred to those of uniform section because these are economical for
explain: Beams of uniform strength save material by removing unnecessary cross-section where bending moment is low, making them more economical particularly for lighter load applications where material savings matter proportionally more.

q: 31. The moment diagram for a cantilever carrying linearly varying load from zero at its free end and to maximum at the fixed end will be
explain: Integrating a linearly varying (triangular) load twice to get the bending moment produces a cubic variation, giving a cubic parabola moment diagram.

q: 32. The moment diagram for a cantilever which is subjected to a uniformly distributed load will be a
explain: For a cantilever under UDL, the bending moment varies quadratically (parabolically) along its length, being zero at the free end and maximum at the fixed end.

q: 33. Shear force for a cantilever carrying a uniformly distributed load over its length, is
explain: For a cantilever under UDL, shear force varies linearly from zero at the free end to maximum at the fixed end, giving a triangular SFD.
